title: Capella vs Liberty: control, tuition, size
summary: Capella University (Capella) versus Liberty University (Liberty). Also searched as Liberty vs Capella. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Capella University and Liberty University differ notably in several aspects. Capella is a private for-profit institution located in Minneapolis, whereas Liberty is a private nonprofit university based in Lynchburg. In terms of undergraduate enrollment, Liberty has a larger student body with 50,012 students compared to Capella's 18,364. Tuition costs also vary, with Capella charging $14,400 for in-state undergraduate tuition, while Liberty's in-state tuition is higher at $22,465. These differences highlight distinct institutional models and scales between Capella University and Liberty University, or Capella vs Liberty.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing cost, Capella University and Liberty University show significant differences. Capella charges $14,400 for both in-state and out-of-state undergraduate tuition, reflecting a consistent tuition rate regardless of residency. In contrast, Liberty University has a higher tuition fee of $22,465 for both in-state and out-of-state students. Regarding student debt, the median debt for Capella graduates who complete their programs is $14,968, whereas Liberty graduates have a higher median debt of $24,500. These figures illustrate the financial considerations prospective students might evaluate when choosing between Capella University and Liberty University, or Capella vs Liberty.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Capella University and Liberty University differ in their learning models and campus settings. Capella University, located in Minneapolis, Minnesota, primarily offers online education with a focus on flexible learning options suitable for working adults. Liberty University, based in Lynchburg, Virginia, provides a traditional campus experience alongside extensive online programs, accommodating a larger undergraduate population. With 18,364 undergraduates at Capella and 50,012 at Liberty, the scale and delivery methods reflect distinct approaches to higher education. These differences underscore the contrast between Capella University and Liberty University, or Capella vs Liberty, in how they structure their academic environments and engage students.

sections.heading: Pick Capella if
paragraphs: Pick Capella University if you prefer a private for-profit institution with a tuition rate of $14,400 for undergraduate studies. Capella offers a flexible learning environment, primarily online, which may suit students balancing education with other commitments. The university's completion rate within 150% of the expected program time is 20%, reflecting the pace at which students finish their degrees. These factors make Capella a consideration for those seeking an accessible and adaptable higher education option.

sections.heading: Pick Liberty if
paragraphs: Pick Liberty University if you are looking for a private nonprofit institution with a high admission rate of approximately 99%. Liberty's undergraduate tuition is $22,465, which is higher than Capella's, reflecting its nonprofit status. The university has a completion rate of about 65% within 150% of the expected program time, indicating a relatively strong student success rate. These attributes make Liberty University a suitable choice for students seeking a nonprofit environment with broad accessibility and a solid track record of degree completion.
